payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are both the mug and the headphones visible enough to compare their positions?
node.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
node.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too broad and its evidence is not grounded in the actual edited image. The edited image shows a mug on the right of the headphones, but also a second mug to their left and a conspicuous blurred blue remnant where the original mug was; this is evidence of partial progress, not complete fulfillment. The current traces merely repeat the right-side relationship and do not check whether the requested move is complete relative to the source or account for the remaining original mug/remnant. Refine the typed binding/criteria to evaluate the requested mug’s movement from the source against the edited snapshot, distinguishing a completed move from partial progress while preserving unknown when identity or evidence is genuinely unclear. Do not treat the two near-identical support observations as independent confirmation: both depend on the same observation path. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; the mismatch is semantic/evidential, and the 0.99 confidence does not resolve it.

The right-side mug supports progress, but these visible leftovers make the simple right-of relation insufficient to establish full fulfillment; preserve partial when evidence supports progress without completion, and unknown only when identity or visual evidence is genuinely unresolved.
